models._description: Point of Sale Payment Methods (online-payment extension)

behavioral_notes.observation: The module turns a pos.payment.method into an 'online' method via is_online_payment plus a m2m online_payment_provider_ids of payment.provider records (empty = all published enabled/test providers). When is_online_payment is set, create/write call _force_online_payment_values which blanks the terminal/journal-bound fields (journal_id, receivable_account_id, outstanding_account_id, use_payment_terminal, qr_code_method, is_cash_count, split_transactions) and forces type='online', payment_method_type='none' -- so the online method deliberately does NOT settle through a POS journal like cash/card. A constraint (_check_pos_config_online_payment + pos.config._check_online_payment_methods) enforces at most one online payment method per pos.config and that its providers share the config currency. This constrained schema-mutation is invisible to field metadata.

PaymentPortal subclasses the core payment portal. GET /pos/pay/<pos_order_id> authorises the order via _document_check_access(access_token), requires the pos.session be 'opened', resolves the partner (falling back to the company public user, else redirect to login), computes amount_to_pay from next_online_payment_amount (or the unpaid balance), intersects the order's online-method providers with _get_compatible_providers, and renders the pos_online_payment.pay payment form. JSONRPC /pos/pay/transaction/<id> re-validates session/amount/provider, forces currency and partner, injects custom_create_values={'pos_order_id': order.id}, disables tokenization for public users, then calls the inherited _create_transaction and sets the tx landing_route back to /pos/pay/confirmation. The amount is re-checked server-side against the order so a customer cannot pay a stale total. All three routes are auth='public' so an unauthenticated phone (e.g. via a scanned link/QR) can pay.

When a transaction reaches authorized/done -- either synchronously at GET /pos/pay/confirmation (which calls tx._process_pos_online_payment after checking tx.pos_order_id matches and state in authorized/done) or asynchronously via the inherited _post_process override -- the module mints the accounting payment (account.payment via _create_payment if account_payment did not already), resolves the order's online pos.payment.method (creating one with _get_or_create_online_payment_method if needed), and calls pos_order.add_payment(...) to write a pos.payment line linked to the account.payment (online_account_payment_id). If the order is still draft and _is_pos_order_paid() it runs _process_saved_order(False) to finalise it (paid -> picking/invoice via base POS). Finally it fires pos.config._notify('ONLINE_PAYMENTS_NOTIFICATION', {'id': order.id}) on the bus so the cashier's OWL terminal does a safe RPC to refresh the order state. This webhook-driven, idempotent feedback from a confirmed transaction into a POS payment line is pure Python and invisible to metadata.

pos.order gains online_payment_method_id (computed from the config's single online method) and next_online_payment_amount (the amount the cashier requests for the next phone payment, validated to be within the unpaid balance). get_and_set_online_payments_data is the RPC the terminal polls to set that amount and read back online payments already made / amount unpaid; if the requested amount is 0 and the order is an empty draft (no online payments, not restaurant, no trusted config) it _clean_payment_lines and deletes the throwaway order created only for the pay flow. _process_order strips any client-supplied online payment lines from draft orders so the online tender is only ever recorded server-side from a real confirmed transaction.

pos.payment.create refuses an online-method payment that has no linked online_account_payment_id (account.payment), and refuses a non-online method that carries one; pos.payment.write blocks editing essential data (amount/date/method/order/account link) of an online payment. _check_payment_method_id only warns (does not block) when the saved online method differs from the order's currently configured one, so a settled online payment is never lost even if the config later changes. These invariants enforce the one-to-one online-payment<->account.payment binding.

The cashier-side experience is OWL/JS: the module adds a single OnlinePaymentPopup component and patches PaymentScreen, OrderPaymentValidation, PosStore, PosOrder and PosPayment plus the CustomerDisplay / CustomerDisplayPosAdapter (so a customer-facing screen can show a QR/link to pay). 9 JS files / 1 XML template across point_of_sale.assets_prod and the customer_display bundles, no new registry services. The screen flow that requests an online payment, shows the pay link/QR and waits for the ONLINE_PAYMENTS_NOTIFICATION bus signal to mark the order paid lives entirely in this client code and is not reverse-engineerable from Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: pos_online_payment (auto-installed bridge: lets a POS customer settle a pos.order online through a payment.provider; backend ORM glue + public payment portal + OWL POS overrides)
software_services: /pos/pay/<pos_order_id> (public payment form for a POS order)
logical_data_erm: pos.order -> pos.payment.method (online_payment_method_id, the single online method on the config)
information_flows: depends: point_of_sale, account_payment (which depends on payment + account)
inbound: customer phone (public) GET /pos/pay -> jsonrpc /pos/pay/transaction -> payment._create_transaction (provider redirect/inline/token)
side-effect: _process_pos_online_payment -> account.payment (_create_payment) + pos.payment line (add_payment) + finalise draft order (_process_saved_order)
bus: pos.config._notify('ONLINE_PAYMENTS_NOTIFICATION') -> cashier OWL terminal refreshes order state via RPC
frontend: cashier requests next_online_payment_amount, shows pay link/QR on PaymentScreen + CustomerDisplay

external_integrations.pattern: No direct outbound HTTP in this module: it reuses the payment engine's providers. The actual acquirer API calls / api-keys live in the underlying payment + payment_<provider> modules; this bridge only selects compatible payment.provider records and drives the transaction lifecycle.
external_integrations.note: gap #7 here is indirect -- external reach is delegated to the payment engine; this module contributes the POS-order binding and settlement feedback.

capabilities: Collect POS Payment Online (customer pays a pos.order from their own phone)
Generate Pay Link / QR for a POS Order
Configure an Online Payment Method (one per till, with allowed providers)
Settle Confirmed Transaction into a POS Payment Line
Reconcile Online POS Payment to an Accounting Payment
value_streams: Pay-POS-Order-Online: cashier requests online tender (next_online_payment_amount) -> show link/QR -> customer opens /pos/pay -> create + confirm payment.transaction at provider -> _process_pos_online_payment writes account.payment + pos.payment -> order marked paid -> bus notifies terminal
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; reuses point_of_sale POS groups and public/portal access for the customer-facing pay routes)
policies: at most one online payment method per pos.config (_check_pos_config_online_payment / pos.config._check_online_payment_methods)
online method providers must share the POS config currency (_get_online_payment_providers error_if_invalid)
online payment lines are never trusted from the client: stripped from draft orders in _process_order and only written server-side from a confirmed transaction
online pos.payment must be 1:1 with an account.payment and is immutable once saved (pos.payment.create/write guards)
pay routes require an opened pos.session and a valid access_token (_check_order_access / _ensure_session_open)
stakeholders: POS Customer / Payer (res.partner or public user, pays on their phone)
Cashier / POS User (requests the online payment at the till)
Payment Provider (external acquirer, via the payment engine)
Accountant (consumes the account.payment + session closing entry)
metrics: online vs total tendered amount per pos.order (amount_paid / amount_unpaid)
payment.transaction state distribution for POS-linked transactions (inherited payment reporting)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: pos_online_payment is an auto-installed bridge whose mission is the omnichannel settlement of a retail counter sale: it lets the customer pay a pos.order from their own phone (scan a link/QR served at the public /pos/pay route) so the till transaction can be marked paid. It is classified with its parent point_of_sale as a value-chain primary activity under APQC 3.0 (Market and Sell): the originating, value-creating act it serves is the in-store sell/checkout transaction, and this module simply moves the tender step onto the customer's device. The payment-engine side it leans on (payment / account_payment) is itself a value-network/support 9.0 collect-cash component, and the confirmed transaction does feed an account.payment (APQC 9.5) -- but those are triggered downstream effects; the dominant operation this module exists to complete is the POS sale, so value_model=chain, activity_class=primary, mirroring point_of_sale rather than payment. It carries strong network overtones (it brokers buyer + acquirer through public mediation routes) but the value logic it completes is the chain sell.

standard_capabilities: one online payment method per till backed by configured payment providers (empty = all published)
public payment portal for a POS order (/pos/pay) usable from a customer phone via shared link/QR
redirect / inline / saved-token payment flows reused from the payment engine
automatic settlement of a confirmed transaction into a pos.payment + account.payment, finalising the order
real-time cashier notification (bus) so the terminal refreshes when the customer pays
currency/amount re-validation server-side to prevent stale or mismatched payments
typical_fits: scan-to-pay at the counter (customer settles their own order on their phone)
split a POS order so part is paid online (next_online_payment_amount)
restaurant table pay-online flow combined with pos_restaurant
any payment provider already supported by an installed payment_<provider> module
common_gaps: the module ships no acquirer: a payment_<provider> module (Stripe, Adyen, etc.) must be installed and a provider published/enabled
all configured providers must share the POS config currency (multi-currency tills need extra setup)
QR/link delivery to the customer is the standard popup/customer-display flow; bespoke kiosk or table-QR UX is OWL dev
no per-provider reconciliation/fee handling beyond what account_payment provides
country-specific fiscal capture of the online tender may need certification add-ons
drive_hints: curl GET /pos/pay/<pos_order_id>?access_token=... (auth=public) to render the POS pay form
